title: House of Anjou-Sicily
capsule: After the Sicilian Vespers revolt of 1282 stripped Charles I of Anjou's dynasty of the island of Sicily, his Angevin heirs retained the mainland provinces from their capital at Naples, still styling themselves kings of Sicily ('citra Pharum,' this side of the strait) even as Aragon ruled the island itself. Charles II (r. 1285-1309) and his son Robert the Wise (r. 1309-1343) built Naples into a major center of Trecento art and learning, patronizing Petrarch and Boccaccio and hosting Giotto's frescoes. The dynasty's fortunes declined under the contested reign of Robert's granddaughter Joanna I (r. 1343-1382), who was deposed by her cousin Charles of Durazzo in 1381 and murdered in 1382, passing the Neapolitan throne to the rival Angevin-Durazzo line amid the War of the Angevin Succession.
